skill.name: azure-quotas
skill.description: Check Azure quota limits, usage, and available regional capacity with Azure CLI workflows. Compare regions and prepare quota increase requests.
skill.summary: Inspect Azure quotas and plan capacity across subscriptions, providers, and regions.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by documented Azure CLI examples, Markdown code formatting, standard error redirection, and expected read-only quota queries. Two semantic risks remain: the scripts install an Azure CLI extension without confirmation, and the Bash script embeds Azure response data directly into Python source.

remediation.issue: The quota scripts automatically install the Azure CLI quota extension.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before extension installation, or exit with a clear prerequisite command.

remediation.issue: The Bash script interpolates Azure JSON output into a Python source string.
remediation.suggestion: Pass both JSON documents through standard input, environment variables, or files and parse them only as data.

remediation.issue: Quota increase guidance does not require confirmation before a cloud account change.
remediation.suggestion: Preview the subscription, scope, resource, and requested limit, then require explicit confirmation before running update or create commands.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Azure CLI Extension Installation
semantic_findings.description: Both scripts install the quota extension automatically when absent. This downloads code and changes the local Azure CLI environment without explicit confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The installation commands and automatic branches are explicit in both scripts.

semantic_findings.title: Azure Response Embedded in Python Source
semantic_findings.description: The Bash script interpolates quota usage JSON into a triple-quoted Python source string. Crafted response content could break the string and alter executed Python.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Direct interpolation into the python3 -c program is visible, although exploitation requires control over Azure CLI response content.

content.user_title: Check Azure Quotas and Regional Capacity
content.value_statement: Azure deployment plans can fail when regional quotas are unknown or exhausted. This skill checks limits and usage, compares regions, and guides increase requests.
actual_capabilities: Lists quotas for Azure resource providers and regional scopes.
Retrieves current usage and calculates available capacity.
Checks one named quota or summarizes all quotas in a scope.
Compares quota availability across candidate Azure regions.
Guides quota increase requests and request status checks.
limitations: Requires an authenticated Azure CLI session and permission to read the target subscription.
The supplied scripts may install the Azure CLI quota extension.
Some Azure resource providers do not support the quota API.
Quota values reflect the selected subscription and can change after the check.

use_cases.title: Validate Deployment Capacity
use_cases.description: Check whether a planned workload fits available quota before selecting a region.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Quota Failures
use_cases.description: Compare current usage with limits when an Azure deployment reports a quota error.

use_cases.title: Plan Quota Increases
use_cases.description: Review current capacity and prepare a scoped quota increase request for approval.

prompt_templates.title: Check Regional Compute Quotas
prompt_templates.prompt: Check all Microsoft.Compute quotas in eastus for my current Azure subscription. Show each limit, current usage, and available capacity.

prompt_templates.title: Validate One Resource Quota
prompt_templates.prompt: Check <resource-name> for <provider> in <region> using subscription <subscription-id>. Explain whether <required-capacity> additional units fit.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Candidate Regions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare <resource-name> quota across <region-list>. Rank regions by available capacity and identify any region that meets <required-capacity>.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Increase Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a quota increase plan for <resource-name> in <region>. Show current values and the exact scope. Do not submit changes until I confirm.

output_examples.input: Compare 100 available vCPUs across eastus, eastus2, and westus2.
output: eastus2 meets the requirement with 180 available vCPUs.
westus2 meets the requirement with 120 available vCPUs.
eastus does not meet the requirement with 60 available vCPUs.

output_examples.input: Plan an increase to 500 DSv3 family vCPUs in eastus.
output_examples.output: Current limit and usage are shown first. The proposed request targets 500 vCPUs and waits for confirmation before submission.

best_practices: List quotas first to discover the exact Azure quota resource name.
Verify the active subscription and regional scope before reading or changing quota.
Confirm the requested limit and scope before submitting any quota increase.
anti_patterns: Do not infer quota resource names from ARM resource types.
Do not treat a No Limit response as proof of unlimited capacity.
Do not submit quota increases without explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: What permissions are required?
faq.answer: Reader access supports quota checks. Quota Request Operator or equivalent permissions are required for increase requests.

faq.question: Does the skill require Azure CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflows use Azure CLI and the quota extension.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple regions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can check the same quota across candidate regions and compare available capacity.

faq.question: Can it request a quota increase?
faq.answer: It provides Azure CLI guidance for increase requests. Confirm the subscription, scope, and requested limit before submission.

faq.question: Why does the quota API return BadRequest?
faq.answer: The selected resource provider may not support the Microsoft.Quota API. Use official service limits documentation as a fallback.

faq.question: Does a No Limit value mean unlimited capacity?
faq.answer: No. It can indicate unsupported or unavailable quota data. Check service-specific limits and regional capacity.
